text.p: John Krol, DuPont Co chief executive officer, was paid a 1996 salary of $900,000, up 28 percent from 1995, and received an additional $1.5 million in bonuses, a regulatory filing Friday showed.
In a proxy filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, DuPont said Krol's raise reflected the first full year of substantially increased responsibilities.

In evaluating Krol's performance, DuPont's compensation committee noted the company's record earnings, 38 percent shareholder return, and Krol's leadership in continuing to position DuPont for long-range profitable growth.
In 1996 DuPont granted Krol, 60, a stock option on 103,000 shares with an exercise price of $79.25 a share, the filing said.
In January 1997 he received an option on 291,500 more shares with an exercisable price of $150 per share.
Edgar Woolard Jr, 63, who has retired as a DuPont employee but remains chairman of the board and chairman of the Strategic Direction Committee, receives $300,000 a year, the filing said.
